title: Apple Pie
description: Classic American apple pie with tender cinnamon apples baked inside a flaky double crust.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and place a rimmed baking sheet on the lower rack so it becomes hot enough to catch drips and help the bottom crust brown.
Roll one dough disk into a circle large enough for a 9-inch pie plate, ease it into the plate without stretching, and refrigerate while preparing the filling.
Toss the sliced apples with both sugars, flour, lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until every slice is lightly coated and glossy.
Pile the apples into the chilled crust, mounding them slightly in the center, and dot the surface with small pieces of butter for richness.
Roll the second dough disk, place it over the apples or cut it into lattice strips, then seal and crimp the edges firmly so juices stay inside.
Brush the top crust with egg wash, sprinkle with coarse sugar if using, and cut several vents if the top crust is solid.
Bake for 20 minutes at 425°F, then reduce to 375°F and bake 40 to 45 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles thickly.
Cool the pie on a rack for at least 3 hours before slicing so the apple juices set instead of running across the plate.
tips: Use a mix of tart and sweet apples for balanced flavor.
Keep dough cold for a flakier crust.
Wait for visible bubbling before removing the pie.
commonMistakes: Stretching dough into the pan can make it shrink.
Underbaking leaves floury filling and pale bottom crust.
Slicing too soon makes the filling watery.
substitutions: Use store-bought pie dough if needed.
Replace nutmeg with allspice for a warmer aroma.
Use tapioca starch instead of flour for a clearer filling.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day.
Refrigerate leftovers for up to 4 days.
Rewarm slices in a 325°F oven until the crust crisps slightly.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Pumpkin Pie
description: Silky pumpkin custard pie baked in a flaky crust with warm fall spices.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F, fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate, crimp the edge, and chill it while the filling is mixed.
Whisk pumpkin puree and brown sugar together until smooth, breaking up any lumps so the finished custard has an even texture.
Add the eggs and whisk only until combined, because beating in too much air can make the custard puff and crack.
Whisk in evaporated milk, cream, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, and salt until the filling is fluid and evenly spiced.
Place the chilled crust on a rimmed baking sheet, pour in the pumpkin filling, and move it carefully so the liquid does not splash over the edge.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes until the edges are set and the center still has a small gentle wobble when the pan is nudged.
Cool the pie completely on a rack, letting carryover heat finish setting the custard without overbaking the center.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before slicing, then serve chilled or cool with whipped cream added just before serving.
tips: Use pure pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling.
Shield the crust edge if it browns too quickly.
A slight center wobble prevents a dry cracked custard.
commonMistakes: Overwhisking adds air bubbles.
Overbaking can crack the filling.
Using warm crust makes the edge slump.
substitutions: Use half-and-half instead of cream and evaporated milk.
Use pumpkin pie spice instead of individual spices.
Use a graham crust for a softer variation.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooling.
Keep covered for up to 4 days.
Freeze tightly wrapped slices for up to 1 month.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Pecan Pie
description: Classic pecan pie with a flaky crust, toasted pecans, and a glossy caramel-like filling.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, arrange the pie crust in a 9-inch pie plate, crimp the edge, and chill it while preparing the filling.
Spread the pecans in the crust, turning some pretty halves upward so the baked pie has a clearly recognizable pecan surface.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl until smooth, then add corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, salt, and bourbon if using.
Pour the filling slowly over the pecans, pausing if needed so the nuts can settle into an even layer without overflowing.
Place the pie on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 45 to 55 minutes until the edges are puffed and the center jiggles like set gelatin.
If the crust darkens before the filling sets, cover only the edge with foil or a pie shield and continue baking gently.
Cool the pie completely for at least 3 hours so the syrupy filling firms into clean slices instead of spilling out.
Slice with a sharp knife, wiping between cuts, and serve plain or with unsweetened whipped cream to balance the sweetness.
tips: Use fresh pecans because stale nuts taste bitter.
A rimmed baking sheet makes moving the pie safer.
The center should wobble slightly, not slosh.
commonMistakes: Removing the pie while the center is liquid causes runny slices.
Burning the crust edge before the filling sets is common.
Using salted nuts can make the filling too salty.
substitutions: Use dark corn syrup for a deeper molasses flavor.
Replace bourbon with milk or omit it.
Use maple syrup for part of the corn syrup if desired.
storage: Cool completely before covering.
Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Freeze well-wrapped slices for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Key Lime Pie
description: Tangy Key lime pie with a graham cracker crust, creamy citrus filling, and whipped cream.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and mix graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar until the crumbs feel evenly moistened like damp sand.
Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate, using a cup to compact the crust evenly.
Bake the crust for 8 minutes until fragrant and lightly darker, then cool it while keeping the oven on for the filling.
Whisk egg yolks until slightly thickened, then whisk in sweetened condensed milk, Key lime juice, and lime zest until smooth.
Pour the filling into the warm crust and spread it level so the pie bakes evenly and slices cleanly after chilling.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the filling is set around the edges and just barely trembles in the center.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours so the citrus custard becomes cold and sliceable.
Whip cream with powdered sugar, dollop or pipe it on the chilled pie, and garnish with lime slices immediately before serving.
tips: Bottled Key lime juice is acceptable if real Key limes are unavailable.
Compact the crumb crust firmly to prevent crumbling.
Chill fully for the cleanest slices.
commonMistakes: Overbaking can make the filling grainy.
Loose crumbs make the crust fall apart.
Adding whipped cream before chilling can make it weep.
substitutions: Use regular lime juice for a less floral but still tangy pie.
Use digestive biscuits instead of graham crackers.
Use meringue instead of whipped cream if preferred.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days.
Keep whipped cream loosely covered.
Freeze without whipped cream for up to 1 month.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Cheesecake
description: Creamy baked cheesecake with a buttery graham cracker crust and a smooth vanilla filling.
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F, grease a 9-inch springform pan, and wrap the outside tightly with foil if using a water bath.
Mix graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar, then press the crumbs firmly across the bottom and slightly up the sides of the pan.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes and cool it while preparing the filling, keeping the oven temperature steady and gentle.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, and salt on medium-low until completely smooth, scraping the bowl often so no lumps remain.
Add eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing just until each disappears because excess air can puff and crack the cheesecake.
Mix in sour cream and vanilla, pour the batter over the cooled crust, and smooth the top without aggressively tapping the pan.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes until the edges look set and the center still has a soft wobble when gently nudged.
Cool gradually, then refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight before releasing the pan and slicing with a warm clean knife.
tips: Room-temperature cream cheese blends smoothly.
Low-speed mixing reduces cracks.
A long chill is essential for texture.
commonMistakes: Cold cream cheese leaves lumps.
Overmixing after eggs makes the cake rise and crack.
Cutting before chilling gives soft messy slices.
substitutions: Use vanilla wafer crumbs for the crust.
Use Greek yogurt instead of sour cream.
Top with berries, caramel, or chocolate after chilling.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 5 days.
Freeze slices tightly wrapped for up to 2 months.
Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before serving.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: New York Cheesecake
description: Tall, dense New York cheesecake with browned edges, a creamy center, and a crisp crumb crust.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease a 9-inch springform pan, and wrap the outside tightly if baking in a water bath.
Combine graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar, press firmly into the pan, and bake the crust for 10 minutes before cooling.
Reduce the oven to 325°F and beat cream cheese until smooth before adding sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a steady stream.
Mix in sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla on low speed, scraping the bowl so the dense filling stays smooth from top to bottom.
Add eggs and yolks one at a time, mixing only until blended after each addition to avoid adding extra air.
Pour the filling into the crust, smooth the top, and set the pan in a roasting pan with hot water halfway up the sides if using a bath.
Bake 70 to 80 minutes until the edges are puffed and lightly browned while the center still moves as one soft mass.
Turn off the oven, crack the door for 45 minutes, then cool and refrigerate overnight before slicing for the dense New York texture.
tips: Use full-fat brick cream cheese for the densest texture.
Cool slowly to reduce cracking.
Overnight chilling makes the flavor and structure better.
commonMistakes: Using whipped cream cheese changes the texture.
Skipping gradual cooling can split the surface.
Overbaking makes the center dry and crumbly.
substitutions: Use vanilla wafer crumbs for the crust.
Use a small amount of orange zest instead of lemon juice.
Serve with cherry topping on the side.
storage: Refrigerate tightly covered for up to 5 days.
Freeze whole or sliced for up to 2 months.
Thaw in the refrigerator and slice while cold.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Carrot Cake
description: Moist spiced carrot cake layered with tangy cream cheese frosting and toasted nuts.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease two 9-inch cake pans, line the bottoms with parchment, and lightly flour the sides.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, and salt until the leaveners and spices are evenly distributed.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, both sugars, eggs, and vanilla until glossy and fully combined without needing an electric mixer.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture just until a few flour streaks remain so the cake stays tender.
Fold in grated carrots and toasted walnuts, making sure the carrots are spread evenly rather than clumped in one area.
Divide batter between pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes until the centers spring back and a tester comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool the layers in the pans for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely before frosting to prevent melting.
Spread cream cheese frosting between layers and over the cake, then chill briefly before slicing for clean layers.
tips: Grate carrots finely for a tender crumb.
Toast nuts before adding them.
Frost only fully cooled cake layers.
commonMistakes: Pre-shredded carrots are often too dry and coarse.
Overmixing after flour makes the cake tough.
Warm layers melt cream cheese frosting.
substitutions: Use pecans instead of walnuts.
Add raisins if desired.
Use applesauce for part of the oil for a lighter cake.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 5 days.
Bring slices near room temperature before serving.
Freeze unfrosted layers for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Red Velvet Cake
description: Soft red velvet layer cake with a light cocoa flavor and classic cream cheese frosting.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease two 9-inch cake pans, line them with parchment, and dust lightly with flour.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt so the small amount of cocoa is evenly spread through the batter.
In a second bowl, whisk sugar, oil, eggs, buttermilk, vinegar, vanilla, and red coloring until smooth and vivid.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in two additions, folding gently until no dry pockets remain.
Divide the batter evenly between pans and tap once or twice to release only large air pockets without deflating the batter.
Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until the centers spring back and a toothpick comes out with a few moist red crumbs.
Cool the layers fully, then level domed tops if needed and save a few crumbs for decorating the finished cake.
Fill and frost with cream cheese frosting, add reserved crumbs if desired, and chill briefly before slicing cleanly.
tips: Use buttermilk for tenderness and tang.
Measure cocoa lightly so the cake stays red.
Chill the frosted cake briefly for neater slices.
commonMistakes: Too much cocoa turns the cake brown.
Skipping vinegar weakens the classic red velvet tang.
Frosting warm layers causes sliding.
substitutions: Use gel food coloring for stronger color.
Use ermine frosting for a traditional variation.
Use sour milk if buttermilk is unavailable.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 5 days.
Let slices sit 20 minutes before serving.
Freeze unfrosted layers for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Brownies
description: Fudgy chocolate brownies with crackly tops, chewy edges, and rich cocoa flavor.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving overhang so the brownies lift out cleanly.
Melt butter in a saucepan or microwave-safe bowl, then whisk in both sugars while the butter is warm to help create shiny tops.
Whisk in cocoa powder and salt until the mixture looks dark, smooth, and slightly glossy with no dry cocoa pockets.
Add eggs one at a time and whisk firmly after each addition until the batter thickens and becomes shiny.
Stir in vanilla, then fold in flour only until the last streaks disappear so the brownies stay fudgy rather than cakey.
Fold in chocolate chips, spread the thick batter evenly in the pan, and smooth the corners so the slab bakes evenly.
Bake 28 to 32 minutes until the top is crackly and a tester inserted near the center comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool completely before lifting from the pan and slicing with a sharp knife for clean squares and intact fudgy centers.
tips: Warm butter helps dissolve sugar for a shiny crust.
Use a metal pan for defined chewy edges.
Slightly underbake for fudgy centers.
commonMistakes: Overmixing flour makes brownies tough.
A clean toothpick usually means overbaked brownies.
Cutting warm brownies creates ragged edges.
substitutions: Use dark chocolate chips for deeper flavor.
Add walnuts if desired.
Use espresso powder to intensify the chocolate.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.
Refrigerate for firmer fudgy texture.
Freeze squares for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Blondies
description: Chewy brown sugar blondies with buttery vanilla flavor and golden crackly tops.
ingredients: 1 cup white chocolate chips or chopped pecans
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving enough overhang to lift out the slab.
Whisk melted butter and brown sugar until the mixture looks glossy and cohesive, which helps the bars bake chewy.
Add the egg, yolk, and vanilla, then whisk until the batter is smooth and slightly thickened from the extra yolk.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt separately so the small amount of leavener is evenly distributed before mixing.
Fold the dry ingredients into the butter mixture gently until only a few flour streaks remain in the thick batter.
Fold in white chocolate chips or pecans, spread the batter evenly into the pan, and smooth the top to the corners.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until the edges are set, the top is lightly crackled, and the center no longer looks wet.
Cool completely in the pan before lifting out and cutting into squares so the chewy centers hold their shape.
tips: Use packed brown sugar for deep caramel flavor.
Do not overbake; the center firms as it cools.
A parchment sling makes clean removal easy.
commonMistakes: Using hot butter with eggs can scramble them.
Overbaking makes blondies dry and cakey.
Cutting before cooling causes the centers to collapse.
substitutions: Use dark chocolate chips instead of white chocolate.
Add toasted pecans for crunch.
Use browned butter for a nuttier flavor.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.
Refrigerate for a firmer chewy texture.
Freeze squares for up to 2 months.
